notes.v-synonym-02: New item: 'The IT department ___ projectors to staff who meet clients off-site, free of charge and for up to two weeks at a time.' rents / lends / borrows / donates, key B = lends. This is a context item: all four verbs fit the slot on their own, and each distractor is ruled out by its own clue. 'free of charge' rules out rents, 'to staff' rules out borrows (wrong direction), and 'up to two weeks' rules out donates. I did not use the calibrator's informed/announced/explained/mentioned, because it is still decided by the inform + person + that pattern. Projectors, not laptops, because a listening option reads 'Lend her a newer laptop'. Level 2, medium.
notes.v-collocation-02: New item: 'The revised travel policy will ___ effect on July 1, so trips booked after that date must follow the new rules.' come / take / go / make, key B = take. This replaces 'heavy traffic' (calibrator: easier, style 3) with a staple business collocation. 'come into effect' and 'go into effect' are the lures; the stem has no 'into'. I did not use the calibrator's 'extensive road repairs' set, because 'wide road repairs' can be misparsed and 'spacious/roomy' fail at a glance. Level 1, easy.
notes.v-collocation-05: Stem unchanged. The calibrator's fix is applied: the options are now pull / run / strike / lift, and the key moved from A to C = strike. The distractors now have business collocations of their own (run a business, lift a ban). 'Run a balance' exists only as a credit-card phrase and cannot take 'between A and B'. All explanation fields are rewritten. Level 2, medium.
notes.v-synonym-03: New item: 'Guests who ___ additional charges, such as room service or minibar purchases, must settle them at checkout.' suffer / undergo / endure / incur, key D = incur. This is a near-synonym collocation item: all four verbs translate as 承受／遭受, and only incur takes charges. Voluntary purchases rule out suffer. The calibrator's fix kept the reply-to preposition pattern, so I did not use it. Level 3, hard.
notes.v-synonym-01: New item: 'Sales representatives earn a ___ of 4 percent on every contract they sign, in addition to their base salary.' wage / pension / commission / allowance, key C = commission. All four pay nouns fit 'earn a ___', and 'of 4 percent on every contract' decides. The calibrator's raise/rise/climb/grow is still decided by transitivity alone, so I did not use it. Level 1, easy.
notes.v-synonym-05: Not in changeFirst. The old notify item was object-pattern-decided; together with v-synonym-04 it would have made two pattern items in the synonym unit. New item: 'Showroom visits ___ increased after the renovation, jumping 40 percent in the first week and staying at that level for the rest of the year.' markedly / slightly / steadily / temporarily, key A = markedly. This is the set's adverb item and its hard context item. All four fit 'visits ___ increased', and a separate clue rules out each distractor: 40 percent rules out slightly, 'jumping ... first week' rules out steadily, and 'rest of the year' rules out temporarily. Level 3, hard. It is labelled synonym although the options are change-description adverbs, not strict synonyms.
